title: Kaltenbrunn Pilgrimage Church Kaunertal
name: Kaltenbrunn Pilgrimage Church Kaunertal
kurzbeschreibung: Wallfahrtskirche Maria Kaltenbrunn in Kaunertal: the oldest pilgrimage site in the Tiroler Oberland dating back to 1272, featuring a chapel of grace and healing spring.
beschreibung:
Overview

The history-steeped Wallfahrtskirche Kaltenbrunn (Church of Our Lady with the Child) is located at the entrance to the wildly romantic Kaunertal in the Tyrolean municipality of Kaunertal (Bezirk Landeck) at an elevation of around 1,260 metres above sea level. Picturesquely perched on a sunny hillside terrace above the rushing Faggenbach torrent, the church ensemble is revered as the oldest pilgrimage destination in the entire Tiroler Oberland. For more than 750 years, believers, pilgrims, and culture enthusiasts have journeyed to this spiritual sanctuary, renowned for its serene atmosphere and restorative alpine spring.

Chapel of Grace & Sacred Art

The origins of the pilgrimage date back to 1272: a knight named Erbo von Schenkenberg is said to have founded a wooden hermitage and chapel here in penance for past transgressions. The name Kaltenbrunn refers to the ice-cold, mineral-rich mountain spring that emerges directly beneath the church choir and is credited with curative properties. The present architectural ensemble combines Late Gothic elements from the early 16th century with magnificent Early Baroque remodelling. Prominent artistic treasures include the Late Gothic miracle-working image – a limewood-carved Madonna and Child from the early 15th century –, the richly decorated Baroque high altar, and numerous historic votive tablets testifying to miraculous healings and answered prayers. The integrated fountain chapel invites visitors to draw fresh spring water.

Visit & Getting There

Wallfahrtskirche Kaltenbrunn is open year-round during daylight hours freely and free of charge for visits and prayer. Located right next to the church is the historic Gasthaus Kaltenbrunn, which served as a pilgrims' hospice as early as the 18th century. Getting there by car: take the Inntalautobahn A12 or the B180 (Reschenstraße) to Prutz, turn off into the Kaunertal and follow the Kaunertaler Landesstraße for about seven kilometres to Kaltenbrunn (free parking right at the church). By public transport: ÖBB trains to Landeck-Zams station, then take Postbus route 4232 directly to the Kaunertal Kaltenbrunn Kirche stop.

Tips

Access to the pilgrimage church is low-barrier and step-free. Be sure to visit the small fountain chapel behind the choir to taste the crystal-clear Kaltenbrunn spring water. The pilgrimage church also serves as an ideal starting point for rewarding hikes to the Aifner Alm or along the historic Kaunertal Pilgrims' Path.
